I finished a few years of school so I can read the name on a fertilizer bag, but my mother and father taught me everything I know about farming. This sorghum piece is only 0.06 hectares — too small to buy even part of a bag of DAP from the cooperative when I need that cash for food and soap right now. I will put two baskets of cow manure on it like I did last year, and I will plant the seed I saved from last season because I know it sprouts well in this soil. My family will do all the work ourselves — ploughing with our ox, planting, weeding twice, and scaring the birds away — so I do not need to hire anyone.
